judged_text: updateEvent's fallback branch compares destinationCalendar entries against externalCalendarId inside a branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined. Every Google update that reaches the fallback (externalCalendarId null/empty) previously used event.destinationCalendar.externalId; now it passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update, so all such updates fail with a Google API error and reschedules/edits of bookings without a stored externalCalendarId break.

record.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch compares destinationCalendar entries against externalCalendarId inside a branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined. Every Google update that reaches the fallback (externalCalendarId null/empty) previously used event.destinationCalendar.externalId; now it passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update, so all such updates fail with a Google API error and reschedules/edits of bookings without a stored externalCalendarId break.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()` the fallback branch was changed to:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the exact case that takes the fallback), the `find` predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy `externalCalendarId` (typically `null`/`undefined`), so it will not match normal destination calendar entries and yields `undefined`. Previously this branch used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (now the first destination calendar’s externalId). This is a concrete logic regression in the diff that can lead to `selectedCalendar` being undefined in the fallback path and thus calendar updates targeting no explicit calendarId / wrong calendarId downstream.
